note: Track range (voice-breath-range), step 2: slides across the break, on a lip roll down and as a siren, then the same slide on "oo" from a staff. Missing: a tool that draws a sung slide between two notes on an open vowel (lip-roll only asks for a lip roll), so the last block uses a staff with two notes, and its keys put a tenor's first break inside the slide.

exercise.title: Slides across the break
exercise.why: A slide passes through every pitch between two notes, so it carries your voice across the break with no step to jump over: first on a lip roll, which keeps the sound light, then on an open sound.

cells.text:
Press Start below to begin the lip roll: a tone slides from head voice down to chest voice, then you make the same slide on your own while the mic draws your line. Keep the buzz loose and quiet.
On the way down there is a place where your voice wants to flip: that is the break. Let the buzz stay even through it.

Press Start below to begin the lip roll: the tone now slides up and back down, so you cross the break twice in each round. Let the slide get lighter, not louder, as it climbs.
If the buzz stops at the break, start the next slide more quietly.

Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together, and your pitch shows on the staff. Slide from the low {{1}} up to {{5}} and back down, in one unbroken sound like the lip roll. Sing it on "oo".
Once your line climbs without a jump, try the slide a little higher. Use the Stage selector below to change the key, then press Start exercise to start the drone there.
When you change the key, the slide starts higher and still goes from {{1}} up to {{5}}.
_Don't reach for high notes: keep the slide quiet, and stop if your throat tightens._
